about: Limits for release builds on CI's runners (omui-bench --check). Each says why it is there; raising one needs the same.

budgets.name: ui/frame/one-label
budgets.why: M1 acceptance ⑤: a 1000-node interface at 1080p on the CPU renderer holds 60 Hz

budgets.name: ui/frame/hover-sweep
budgets.why: pointer motion over the same interface holds 60 Hz

budgets.name: ui/frame/all-labels
budgets.why: even when every label of the interface changes in one frame

budgets.name: ui/frame/animate-all
budgets.why: a strong-animation framework (D-60): every card of the interface in motion still holds 60 Hz

budgets.name: canvas/pan-1000
budgets.why: canvas-markdown §3.5: panning a wall of 1000 windows costs under 1 ms of CPU a frame (raster aside)

budgets.name: canvas/zoom-sweep-1000
budgets.why: canvas-markdown §3.5: zooming the same wall in and out costs under 1 ms of CPU a frame

budgets.name: canvas/pan-100k
budgets.why: the grid index: a 100,000-node scene pans as cheaply as what is on screen

budgets.name: ui/frame/idle
budgets.why: a frame with nothing to do costs next to nothing

budgets.name: ui/frame/idle
budgets.why: no allocation per frame (AGENTS.md): the steady state allocates nothing

budgets.name: ui/mount
budgets.why: building and laying out the whole interface fits in one frame

budgets.name: agent/snapshot
budgets.why: an agent reads the whole tree of a 1000-node interface without stalling the UI thread

budgets.name: text/paragraph
budgets.why: shaping and breaking stay well under a microsecond and a half per byte

budgets.name: markdown/parse
budgets.why: a Markdown answer parses at 25 MB/s or more: a 40 KB document in under 2 ms (about 10 ns per byte measured)

budgets.name: markdown/stream-token
budgets.why: a streamed token re-parses only the tail: under 5 µs each, so 20 streaming windows cost well under a millisecond a frame

budgets.name: markdown/to-html
budgets.why: copy as HTML of a long answer stays below a millisecond

budgets.name: text/glyph-motion
budgets.why: styling a glyph for a frame of motion stays far below its rasterisation: 2 000 animated glyphs cost under a millisecond

budgets.name: render/effect-particles
budgets.why: the CPU reference of a particle burst stays interactive: a 480 × 320 layer under 10 ms (the GPU path is the fast one)

budgets.name: trace/span-off
budgets.why: tracing that is off is a branch on a relaxed load (D-59): a few cycles even on a shared CI runner, so a frame's spans cost under a microsecond

budgets.name: trace/span-on
budgets.why: recording a span takes no lock and no allocation (D-59)

budgets.name: log/filtered-out
budgets.why: a log record the filter leaves out is not formatted (D-59): a branch on a relaxed load, a few cycles even on a shared CI runner
